abstract: Pangenomes are reshaping gene-family analysis by shifting from single-genome views to pangene families, yet many studies still rely on orthogroups as proxies, overlooking crucial allele- and locus-level diversity. Here, we present a pangene-based and domain-defined framework to construct and analyze nearly 500 pangene families across four major cereals. Compared with single-genome analyses, pangenome-level family membership increases by 59-264%, and many families show pangene accumulation curves that remain far from saturation, indicating that substantial allelic diversity is still uncharacterized even when 320 rice genomes are included. We further quantify family behavior along three complementary dimensions and reveal extensive remodeling of membership and copy-number allocation that is largely invisible when only total family size is considered. Together, this framework and its associated resource provide a foundation for deeper use of plant pangenomes, offering new insight into how evolutionary constraints and diversification shape pangene families.
